THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, PRAYING TO ALLOW THE APPEAL BY SETTING ASIDE THE IMPUGNED JUDGMENT AND AWARD PASSED IN M.V.C.NO.718/2013 DATED 27.07.2015 BY THE PRL. SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MACT AT KALABURAGI.

THESE APPEALS COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Challenging judgment and award dated 27.07.2015 passed by Principal Senior Civil Judge and MACT at Kalaburagi (for short 'tribunal') in MVC no.718/2013, these appeals are filed.
MFA no.202076/2015 is filed by insurer challenging award on liability and MFA no.201723/2015 is filed by claimants for enhancement of compensation.

2. Smt.Sangeeta Bhadrashetty, learned counsel for appellant in MFA no.202076/2015 submitted that appeal was by insurer challenging finding of tribunal on liability, especially, about involvement of insured vehicle in accident.

It was submitted that as per claimants, accident occurred on 06.02.2013, in which Bhimanna @ Bhimaraya is alleged to have died as a result of insured vehicle bearing registration no.KA-39/M-638 running over him due to rash and negligent driving by its driver.
In complaint NC: 2023:KHC-K:7431 given by brother of deceased on same day, no vehicle number was mentioned.
However, based on his further statement recorded on subsequent day naming insured vehicle, charge sheet was filed.
Based mainly on charge sheet, tribunal fastened liability upon insurer and same calls for interference.
It was also submitted that eyewitnesses named in charge sheet, whose statements were produced before tribunal, did not support case of prosecution.
Such statement would cast serious doubt on basis of charge sheet.
Therefore, tribunal was not justified in passing award against insurer.

3. On other hand, Sri Ananth S. Jahagirdar, learned counsel for appellants in MFA no.201732/2015 submitted that admittedly complainant was not an eyewitness and further statement was given by him to police on next day.
Based on said statement, police conducted investigation and drew Ex.P9 - spot mahazar and thereafter filed charge sheet.
It was submitted that proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act were summary in NC: 2023:KHC-K:7431 nature and claimants could rely on police investigation records to substantiate actionable negligence.
Therefore, tribunal was justified in passing award against insurer.
4. On quantum, it was submitted that as on date of accident, deceased was 22 years of age and earning Rs.15,000/- per month as barber.
However, tribunal erroneously considered it at Rs.5,000/- per month and without adding future prospects, and awarding lower compensation under other heads passed award.
Hence, sought enhancement.

5. Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgment and award.

sentences.text:
From above submission and since insurer is in appeal challenging its liability, while claimant is in appeal for enhancement of compensation, following points would arise for consideration:
"1.
Whether tribunal was justified in passing award against insurer?
Whether claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation?"

Point no.1:
7.

To establish actionable negligence against respondents, claimants relied on FIR, Complaint,
Charge Sheet, Motor Vehicle Inspector's Report, Further Statement and Spot Mahazar marked as Exs.P1 to P3, P5- P7 and P9 respectively.
Indeed Ex.P2 - complaint given by brother of deceased does not mention vehicle number.
But further statements as per Exs.P6 and P7 recorded would implicate insured vehicle.
Thereafter, police conducted investigation.
Ex. P9 - Spot Panchanama drawn on 07.02.2013 at 10.15 a.m. mentions accident was caused by unknown vehicle.
Ex. P5 - Motor Vehicle Inspector's Report would indicate that insured vehicle was inspected on 18.02.2013 at Jewargi Police Station.
Though Exs.P6 and P7 statements are recorded on 07.02.2013, whether they were prior to spot panchanama or subsequent is not indicated even in Case Diary.
When eye witnesses, based on whose statements charge sheet was filed by police, did NC: 2023:KHC-K:7431 not support prosecution case in criminal case
, whether same would be relied upon by Tribunal for purposes of holding actionable negligence against insured vehicle would require consideration.
Evidence on record is inconclusive as to basis for implication of insured vehicle.

Without sufficient basis for holding actionable negligence against driver of insured vehicle, especially when neither investigating officer nor any other eye witnesses are examined by claimants, finding of tribunal about involvement of insured vehicle and liability of insurer based only on Charge Sheet would not be justified.
Matter would require further evidence for said purposes.

Insofar as decision relied upon by learned counsel for claimants in MFA no.30746/2009 (MV) C/W MFA no.30633/2009, it is seen that same would be ratio for proposition that non-examination of eye witnesses in Criminal Cases would not be fatal before tribunal.

However, failure of said eye witness to support NC: 2023:KHC-K:7431 prosecution case in Criminal Case would seriously dent basis on which charge sheet was filed, consequently, casting it under suspicion.
Under such circumstances, impugned award is required to be set-aside and matter remitted back to tribunal with liberty parties to lead further evidence.
Point no.1 is answered partly in affirmative as above.

Point no.2:
8.
In view of finding on point no.1, consideration of point no.2 would not be required.
Parties would be at liberty to re-agitate before tribunal on quantum also.
Hence, point no.2 is answered as not surviving for consideration.

Consequently, following:
